title: Teaching other instruments; Joe Valadie
summary: He taught several instruments and recalls trumpeter Joe Valadie leaving lessons too early.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: You taught all the different instruments, the instruments, clarinet too? Yeah, clarinet and everything.

Clarinet, violin, and uh. Well you played violin for a while. Yeah, I played a little bit. Did you play much on the others? On the others ones, yeah. Trumpet, yeah. I played trumpet and lots and bass fiddle, bass drum, bass horn. I never, you know, kept them for a regular, but I had to know them. Sure. You know, I had to know them. So. Yeah. That's it. So I just kept on, got them all down, worked out. And I got some good, I put some good bands together. I want to sing about these boys, these young boys. They don't, they don't, they don't stay long enough to learn what they ought to learn. Before, if they learn how to play the blues or something, and get a couple of breaks, and play a couple of diminishes, he's gone. Think they know what they're going to do? Yeah, they think he knows something. See, he's gone. I had a boy by the name of Joe Valadie. He was a nice trumpet player. He went on himself. After he got his 15th lesson, he went on. I couldn't hold him, see, he went on. But he come back, see, and I wouldn't fool with him. I wouldn't, because I knew he would have been too good a trumpet player if he had stayed and took what I wanted to give him. But he got out there too early. Then after he got out there early, the brothers told him, say, you ought to have stayed under that man. You should have went, stayed there and learned something. See, he couldn't read good enough, you know, to stay with them big shots, you know. They told him, say, you should have stayed under the man you was under, and you would have been able to play. And he come back with, I wouldn't fool with him. I told him, I said, Mr. Best, I wouldn't fool with you. I said, because you had a chance to learn trumpet and do what you wanted, put up your own band. If you learn how to play good, I said, you could hire fellas. He said, that's right. He said, I'm sorry. I said, I wouldn't fool with you. Take a lesson today and maybe day after tomorrow or next weekend or something like that.
